hero.title: Uveal Melanoma Clinical Registry
hero.one_liner: The clinical registry for the Alberta Ocular Brachytherapy Program. The field list is public. Patient data leave the program only after a request is approved.

snapshot: The registry is for adults treated in the Alberta Ocular Brachytherapy Program. Ezekiel Weis, MD, MPH, leads the clinic. Trafford Crump, PhD, leads the research.
It holds diagnosis and tumour details, brachytherapy and enucleation, imaging, gene-expression results, metastasis and death, ultraviolet exposure, and the questionnaires used in the program.

The questionnaires are PROM-UM, EQ-5D-5L, VF-14, and a surgical-experience survey. PROM-UM has its own page. The code book names the EQ-5D-5L, VF-14, and surgical-experience fields, and it does not reprint that item wording.
The code book and an empty database schema are in a public repository. A fork gives you the structure. It does not give you patients.
Another centre can ask for a de-identified extract. We have not posted a completion rate, a clinic volume, or a price.

why.clinic: We use the registry so the program's clinical data and questionnaires sit in one place, for the clinic and for outcomes research. Collecting PROM-UM and EQ-5D-5L is not a claim that a score changes treatment. This is one provincial program, not a live multi-site network.
why.sponsors: If you need a de-identified extract, email the question, your name and institution, whether ethics approval is in hand or still pending, and the fields you need. Take the field names from the code book. Ezekiel Weis and Trafford Crump read academic and industry requests. A request is not an approval. Any charge is a cost-recovery quote for preparing and transferring that extract, sent through the university. We do not take payment on this page. Biospecimens are not available through this request.

whats_public.note: The field list and an empty database. No patient rows. Forking it does not release data, and a merged change does not write to the clinic.

whats_public.note: What PROM-UM measures, and where registration and licensing are handled.

whats_public.label: PROM-UM psychometric validation
whats_public.note: Weis et al., Cancers, 2023. The psychometric paper. It is not a registry protocol.

whats_public.label: Quality-of-life interviews that informed PROM-UM
whats_public.note: Kopp, Crump, and Weis, Canadian Journal of Ophthalmology, 2017.

non_claims: Nothing on this page is a download of patient data.
We have not published a completion rate, a minimally important difference, an action band, or a clinic volume.
A multi-site registry is not operating. Use by another centre would be a separate agreement.
This is not a cleared device, and it is not a digital therapeutic.
The page shows no row-level data and no chart screenshot.
Collecting PROM-UM and EQ-5D-5L does not mean a score changes treatment.

engage.ask: Request a de-identified extract, or propose a correction to the field list on GitHub. Merging a pull request does not change the clinical registry.
If your program wants the same structure, fork the repository. If you want data from this program, send the request described above.
PROM-UM licensing stays on the PROM-UM page. A registry extract for a sponsored study uses the same request. The quote can differ from an academic request. We still do not publish a price.
